To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the thermal aggregation of acid-hydrolysed β-lg was promoted by hydrolysis, and that the hydrolysis promoted aggregation was likely due to noncovalent and not covalent interactions.

acid hydrolysis of β-lactoglobin and pepsin hydrolysis of acid-hydrolysed β-lactoglobin both promoted thermal aggregation of the protein, and the aggregation was more pronounced with pepsin hydrodlysed β-lacoglobulin.
pepsin hydrolysis of acidified powdered whey ingredients at pH 3-4 increases the viscosity of the dispersions and promotes thermal aggregation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of disulfide bonds and hydrolysis in β-lg aggregation.
the effects of disulfide bonds and hydrolysis of whey proteins on the thermal aggregation at pH 3 and 2.
the effects of acid hydrolysis on thermal aggregation of β-Lg at pH 3-4.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acid hydrolysis of β-lg promotes thermal aggregation of the protein at pH 3, but the mechanism is unclear.
the hydrolytic cleavage of β-lg by pepsin promotes β-lg thermal aggregation at pH 3 and 2.
the hydrolysis of β-lacto globulin at low pH (pH 2) is an important factor in the aggregation process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thermal aggregation of pepsin hydrolyzed β-lg is more rapid compared to acid hydrolyzed β-Lg.
hydrolysis and disulfide interactions are important for the thermal aggregation of acidified β-lg at acidic pH.
acid hydrolysis, disulfide interactions as well as noncovalent associations play a role in defining the functional properties of β-lg at acidic pH.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the thermal aggregation of acid-hydrolysis β-lg is driven mainly by acid hydrolysis rather than disulfide interactions.
the aggregation of β-lg is promoted by pepsin hydrolysis, but the extent of this effect depends on the degree of hydrolysis and the pH.
the presence of disulfide bonds and hydrolysis can affect the thermal aggregation behavior of β-lg.
